summary: R3-NEW-MAJ-001 (correctness) is verifiably closed: `onboarded-operator-bump` is now enumerated as a third cascade-status value across invariant 2, §5.2 item (2), §6 024B acceptance row, and R-024-07 — all four loci required by R3's recommendation. However, fix-round-3 introduced two new MAJ-level correctness defects by editing invariant 2 / §5.2 / §6 024B without updating two prose sections that carry the old two-value model. R4 CANNOT pass with 0 new MAJ: R4-NEW-MAJ-001 (R-024-06 mitigation stale) and R4-NEW-MAJ-002 (§3 protocol position unconditional invocation-log claim) are both introduced by fix-round-3 edits.

findings.title: R3-NEW-MAJ-001 (correctness) closure: onboarded-operator-bump enumerated consistently across invariant 2, §5.2, §6 024B, and R-024-07
findings.evidence:
Four loci verified against plan-doc at d13157f:

(1) **Invariant 2 (plan-doc line 44–47):** The CI enforcement paragraph now names three values in the enum header — `onboarded`, `onboarded-operator-bump`, `blocked-on-adopter-conflict` — and enumerates a distinct bulleted check-path for each. The `onboarded-operator-bump` bullet (line 46) reads: 'PR MUST modify `docs/reviews/WP-SCP-020/branch-protection-log.md` (target match as above) AND STATUS.md MUST contain a row matching the standardised prefix `TF-024X-renovate-<adopter-slug>`.' This is a well-specified third path distinct from both the Renovate path (log entry required, no TF row required) and the conflict path (log NOT modified, TF-conflict reference required).

(2) **§5.2 item (2) (plan-doc lines 116–121):** The DISPATCH-NOTE field spec now explicitly says '**three** values' and defines all three with prose descriptions. `onboarded-operator-bump` is defined at line 118: 'R-024-07 fallback path; an `enable-required-check.sh` invocation occurred + the log entry is in this PR + bake satisfied via operator-driven SHA pin bump (NOT Renovate); STATUS.md gains a `TF-024X-renovate-<adopter-slug>` row gating Threshold A credit (per R-024-07).' Internally consistent with invariant 2.

(3) **§6 024B acceptance row (plan-doc line 190):** The acceptance criterion for `check-invocation-log-entry.sh` now enumerates all three close-states: 'for `onboarded`: requires log entry + target match; for `onboarded-operator-bump`: requires log entry + target match + `TF-024X-renovate-<adopter-slug>` STATUS.md row; for `blocked-on-adopter-conflict`: requires `TF-024X-conflict-<adopter>` reference AND asserts log file was NOT modified.' All three paths present.

(4) **R-024-07 (plan-doc line 209):** Declares `cascade-status: onboarded-operator-bump` as the DISPATCH-NOTE signal for the Renovate-miss path, specifies the TF-row standardised prefix, and closes '024A R3 R3-NEW-MAJ-001 (correctness — third cascade-status value enumerated).' Internally consistent with invariant 2 and §5.2.

All four loci required by R3's recommendation are present and internally consistent. R3-NEW-MAJ-001 (correctness) is CLOSED.

findings.title: R-024-06 mitigation describes a two-value CI check-path model that contradicts invariant 2's three-value negative-assertion model
findings.evidence:
**R-024-06 mitigation (plan-doc line 208)** reads: 'The CI invocation-log check (invariant 2 carve-out) **skips log-entry assertion** for these close-state slices but verifies the TF reference is present.'

This description was accurate under the two-value model that existed before fix-round-3: the CI script had a 'carve-out' that simply skipped the log-entry check for `blocked-on-adopter-conflict` slices and verified the TF reference instead. Fix-round-3 changed the semantics in invariant 2 and §5.2: the CI script now does NOT 'skip' the log-entry check — it actively **asserts the log file was NOT modified** (invariant 2 line 47: 'PR MUST NOT modify `docs/reviews/WP-SCP-020/branch-protection-log.md`'; §6 024B line 190: 'asserts log file was NOT modified'). These are materially different behaviours:

- 'Skip log-entry assertion' = CI is silent about whether the log was modified; only TF reference verified.
- 'Assert log file was NOT modified' = CI actively rejects the PR if the log WAS modified; TF reference also required.

R-024-06's mitigation still says 'skips log-entry assertion' — which describes the OLD behaviour that R3-NEW-MAJ-001 (safety) identified as a bypass surface. The fix-round-3 edit closed that bypass by converting the skip into a negative assertion, but did not update R-024-06. As a result, R-024-06 now describes a CI behaviour that is weaker than what invariant 2 specifies. A reader implementing the CI script from R-024-06 alone would build the weaker (bypassable) version. The fix-round-3 edit created an internal inconsistency between the definitive spec (invariant 2 + §6 024B) and the risk-table row (R-024-06) for exactly this close-state.
findings.recommendation: Update R-024-06 mitigation sentence to replace 'The CI invocation-log check (invariant 2 carve-out) skips log-entry assertion for these close-state slices but verifies the TF reference is present' with language consistent with invariant 2: 'The CI `check-invocation-log-entry.sh` script applies the `blocked-on-adopter-conflict` check-path per invariant 2: it asserts the `branch-protection-log.md` was NOT modified in the PR diff (no invocation occurred) AND verifies the `TF-024X-conflict-<adopter>` TF reference is present in DISPATCH-NOTE.' The phrase 'carve-out' should be retired in this context — it was accurate for the old skip-model but is misleading for the new negative-assertion model.

findings.title: §3 protocol position unconditionally claims SCP-side cascade slices ship an invocation-log entry, contradicting invariant 2 for blocked-on-adopter-conflict close-state
findings.evidence:
**§3 (plan-doc line 73)** describes the SCP-side cascade slice PR as shipping '(a) the cascade slice's DISPATCH-NOTE, **(b) the invocation-log entry under `docs/reviews/WP-SCP-020/branch-protection-log.md`**, (c) any SCP-side ADOPT-001 / scaffolder amendments.' This is stated unconditionally — the sentence applies to 'each adopter cascade slice' with no carve-out for the `blocked-on-adopter-conflict` close-state.

However, after fix-round-3, invariant 2 (line 47) specifies that for `cascade-status: blocked-on-adopter-conflict` slices, 'PR MUST NOT modify `docs/reviews/WP-SCP-020/branch-protection-log.md`' — i.e. no invocation-log entry is shipped; the CI script now **actively enforces** absence of modification. §5.2 item (2) (line 122) also correctly carves this out: 'invocation log entry (D-035) — **only when `cascade-status: onboarded` or `onboarded-operator-bump`**.' 

So §3, §5.2, and invariant 2 are mutually inconsistent: §3 says every cascade-slice ships item (b); §5.2 line 122 says item (b) is conditional; invariant 2 says item (b) is forbidden for one close-state. A first-time reader of §3 (the protocol-position section, typically read first) will form an incorrect model of what conflict-close slices ship, and may file an invocation-log entry when none occurred — triggering the CI negative-assertion failure that invariant 2 is specifically designed to catch.

This inconsistency existed in the pre-fix-round-3 text to a lesser degree (the old two-value model didn't have a negative assertion), but the fix-round-3 promotion of the log-NOT-modified requirement to a hard CI assertion makes the §3 unconditional claim actively misleading at implementation time. The fix-round-3 edit elevated the severity of this pre-existing gap to MAJ.
findings.recommendation: Update §3 line 73 to condition item (b) on the cascade-status close-state. Suggested replacement for '(b) the invocation-log entry under `docs/reviews/WP-SCP-020/branch-protection-log.md`': '(b) the invocation-log entry under `docs/reviews/WP-SCP-020/branch-protection-log.md` **when `cascade-status: onboarded` or `onboarded-operator-bump`** — NOT included for `cascade-status: blocked-on-adopter-conflict` close-state slices (per invariant 2; CI asserts absence of modification for that close-state)'. This makes §3 consistent with §5.2 line 122 and invariant 2 line 47.
